To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the release of IB from minitablets was not dependent on the amount of the water used in the preparation of the complexes.

the dissolution rate of IB from minitablets was not dependent on the amount of βCD used in the formation process, the method used to form the complexes (suspension/solvent, spray-drying, freeze-drying or kneading), or the compaction force applied.
the method used for the preparation of β-cyclodextin complexes does not influence the release of ibuprofen from minitablets or capsules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new pharmaceutical dosage forms (capsules and minitablets) from the complexation of IB with βCD and the comparison of IB release in different media.
the influence of different methods used in the preparation of complexes of IB with βCD on the release of the IB.
the influence of the method of complexation on the release of IB from minitablets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the release of IB is not dependent on the method of the formation of the complex.

the method of preparation of the complex (suspension, solution or kneading) has a significant influence on the release characteristics, and that this is more pronounced in minitablets than in capsules.
the dosage form is not a factor that affects the release of the drug from the complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the release of IB is not dependent on the method of formation of the complexes and that the dosage forms used (minitablets or capsules) are not relevant.

the release of IB from minitablets is dependent on the characteristics of the particle (dependent on the complexation method) and the compaction force, while the release of IB for the capsules is dependent on the method of formation of the complex and the presence of a coating.
the method of complex formation of IB with βCD is not a decisive factor for the release of the IB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method of complex formation of IB with βCD has no influence on the IB release profile from minitablets or capsules.
the method used for the formation of the IB complex has a significant influence on the release of the drug.
the complexation methods and not the dosage form influence the dissolution of IB.
